Subject: POC kickoff: interactive prompt review + routing/load-test session (proposed slots)

Hi Anna —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. To keep momentum on the DataWave POC, I sketched an initial plan for the hands-on prompt review + routing/load-test portion of the kickoff: focus on prompt inventory + structured-output alignment for your most common intents, then a short routing/latency run and a single-nightload test window.

Proposed options (pick one or suggest alternatives):
- Option A: Split workshop across two 90-minute sessions (Americas-friendly):
  * Tue Oct 5, 09:30–11:00 PT — prompt inventory + guardrails, stakeholders + prompt owners
  * Wed Oct 6, 09:30–11:00 PT — routing decisions, structured-output conformance, and quick routing smoke tests
  * Night load test: Wed Oct 6, 22:00–23:30 PT (optional)
- Option B: Single 3-hour block (deep dive, fewer context switches):
  * Thu Oct 7, 08:00–11:00 PT — full workshop then follow-up load test window as needed

Attachments: POC_agenda_v1.pdf (outline, prompt inventory template, guardrails checklist).

Goal for the sessions: leave with a prioritized prompt set, structured-output examples we can validate automatically, and a routing policy to try in the Dedicated pool during the load window.

Cc'ing Ben and Monica for ops/runbook input and Lauren for enablement materials. If we split sessions, we can make the second one narrower for engineers and run the load test at night to avoid impacting traffic.

Best,
Karthik
--

2) Procurement/security asked me to loop them in — they want the standard SOC2 evidence and a short blurb on data retention during the POC before they sign off on the night load test.

Proposed from our side:
- Fri Oct 8, 08:00–09:30 PT — prompt inventory (global owners, high-level)
- Mon Oct 11, 09:30–11:00 PT — engineer session (routing + structured output tests)
- Night load test: Tue Oct 12, 23:00–00:30 PT (DataWave prefers a later window)

I'll hold those tentative on our calendar if that helps. Adding Procurement and SecOps to the thread.

Thanks,
